I really, really love this game.
Now. I will admit, it can be lacking at times. The combat can be a bit iffy at times. The sfx are somewhat meh, and many of the weapons can lack impact, to the point that it feels rather unsatisfying to play at times.
HOWEVER!
The mood is absolutely stunning. The music is beautiful (Mili is my favorite band ever lol so I'm kinda biased), the visual designs are great, the story is very interesting (if somewhat lacking in presentation and clarity, but I do really love piecing together stories like this, so I personally enjoyed the dark souls-esque note finding), and overall it's just a great vibe.
If you want a (mostly) easy grimdark fantasy game that's pretty fair but decently interesting and entertaining, this game would serve you pretty well. I 100%ed it somewhat fast, but I also got it on sale, so it was still basically 1$/hr. Maybe not worth it for everyone at full price, but if it's on sale, I think it's a good buy!

Rough around the edges with major problems regarding the balance of skills and abilities, but really an incredibly beautiful game with wonderful art, design, music and spirit. I enjoyed getting 100% greatly and look forward to any game from the developer in the future!

A Challenging and Story Rich Game

You may find other reviews saying that this game is too hard especially since there are locked doors, enemies scaling up with your level and there being too many documents instead of weapons. But I personally had no issues with the challenges as it is a metroidvania and usually with these types of games, they would not only require you to hack-and-slash but also to strategize your moves.

I must admit that there is a notable skill gap between the bosses and they can definitely one shot you if you aren't in a good level against them but that doesn't really need much exp grinding compared to other games that would take you 5 hours to get to the desired level.

I definitely recommend the game and would recommend it even to beginners/new players of the genre. It is beautiful, and very underrated.

It's a mix of Metroidvania and the souls games, but without the punishing death system. The combat system is very robust and feels as such.
You can find and equip relics to get new abilities and attacks and upgrade them to mix and match attacks.
Other than that it's a standard Metroidvania game, with a beautiful soundtrack.

This is an amazing game if the sound of a Souls-like Metroidvania intrigues you. The atmosphere is very dour, which the art represents in a hauntingly beautiful manner. The game has you collect spirits from Bosses and Midbosses to equip for a variety of different attacks, giving you a large array of choices to fit your ideal playstyle. Since everyone is pretty much dead or undead, alongside the mute protagonist, there is not much direct interaction in the game for story. It is told through apocalypse logs, memories, and background details, although there are still poignant interactions from your helper umbral spirit. The game is also quite difficult, so you have to get a keen sense of attack timing from both your spirits and the enemies to last.

Ender Lilies is one of those games that feels awful to play when you first start, but really opens up once you start unlocking abilities, so for anyone on the fence about the game, stick it out for the first 3-4 bosses until you unlock a decent arsenal. The rest of the game, aside from some issues with level design, is top tier, the plot is great, the music is incredible, yet none of it overstays it's welcome. It's a challenging but fun 20ish hours.

Melancholy metroidvania.

Pro
- Cohesive plot told through journals and cutscenes.
- Competent and responsive platforming. Some tricky optional jumps if going for 100%.
- Area bosses join as a 'basic attack' and minibosses join as a 'skill'. They appear in their actual forms when resting or when you stop moving for a bit.
- Effort has been made to make boss encounters memorable. There's foreshadowing of area boss identities; miniboss encounters have unique attacks and are typically off the critical path.
- Bosses and enemies are mostly unique. There aren't any recycled attacks, though two or three get upgraded in later areas.
- Beautiful levels. Several layers of parallax.
- Soundtrack contributes to level mood. Also Mili.

Con
- Can be difficult to distinguish between your skills and enemy attacks.
- Enemy damage is high. Contact damage feels slightly unfair.

A very polished and deep Metroidvania. Not exactly as hard as a Souls-like (there’s pretty much no penalty for dying), not exactly as easy as the first games of its kinds (some boss battles are brutal), Ender Lilies is a great game. It does everything we expect from a Metroidvania: smooth gameplay, skill-based combat, multiple weapons, amazing soundtrack, and a very large map with multiple secrets. In addition, Ender Lilies stands out due to some unique features: very deep and compelling lore, a very different weapon system, and a strong focus on quality of life features.

This is one of the best games I have played this year; if you like Metroidvanias, definitely get this one.

A beautiful game, with an excellent soundtrack, and generally good boss design. There are some occasional frustrating moments when finding secrets, but those are easily ignored in the whole scheme of the game. The controls feel good and responsive, and most of your deaths feel like your own fault. One of my favorite Souls-Like games.

This game is gorgeous and challenging, but I'm on the verge of putting it down due to a repeating fatal error with the Unreal Engine. It's a known issue, apparently. The only fix I could find that actually worked was installing the enormous Unreal engine from Epic, which eats up all my hard drive space. Going to try uninstalling and reinstalling the game in the hopes that that will do SOMETHING. I hate to let this one go, especially after beating Dark Witch Elene, who was a massive pain in my butt.

The soundtrack alone makes the game an automatic 10/10. Art style is incredibly gorgeous and the gameplay is quite unusual for a souls-like game. I'd say this is more like Persona-meet-Dark-Souls with all of the spirits that you can collect. The somber storyline are flawlessly told through the notes and encounter and enhanced even further the aesthetic and the tone used around the world.

Don't be discouraged by the souls-like tag though. I think the difficulty is actually quite fair and Lily can take quite a punishment before she went down unlike the actual Dark Souls. I don't think I've met any harsh encounter that makes me stuck given the abundant save points across the map.

I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game. It was quite slow to start due to the lack of options, but once I started unlocking options I was hooked. Unfortunately it's lacking some modern QOL options like the ability to take notes on the map so you know what to come back to when you get particular powerups, and the game is pretty linear. While there is a point in the game where multiple routes become available to you, progression is locked behind powerups in all but one area at a time, which is somewhat frustrating. However, all told, I enjoyed this game and 100%ed it and will be looking into the followup for sure.
